title: Logical Backups: pg_dump & pg_restore
description: Export databases with pg_dump custom format (-Fc), perform parallel backups (-j), and restore selectively with pg_restore.

data.text: **`pg_dump`** is the standard logical backup utility for PostgreSQL. It takes a consistent snapshot of the database without blocking read or write operations.

data.title: Parallel Dump and Selective Restore
data.content: Exporting with compression and multi-core parallelism.
data.code:
# 1. Export in custom compressed format using 4 parallel CPU jobs
pg_dump -h localhost -U postgres -d production_db -Fc -j 4 -f prod_backup.dump

# 2. Restore entire database using parallel restore
pg_restore -h localhost -U postgres -d target_db -j 4 --clean --if-exists prod_backup.dump

# 3. Restore only a single specific table from the backup file
pg_restore -h localhost -U postgres -d target_db -t customers prod_backup.dump

data.text: The custom format (`-Fc`) can be restored with `pg_restore`, which supports parallel jobs, selective object restore, and dependency ordering. That is why it is preferred over plain SQL dumps for anything larger than a small database. The directory format (`-Fd`) is similar but writes one file per table and also restores in parallel.

data.title: Dump, list, and restore selectively
data.content: The dump is parallel and compressed; `pg_restore -l` lists objects so you can restore a single table or exclude one.
data.code:
# Parallel custom-format dump
pg_dump -Fc -j 4 -d app -f app.dump

# List the archive contents
pg_restore -l app.dump | head -20

# Restore everything in parallel into a new database
createdb app_restored
pg_restore -j 4 -d app_restored app.dump

# Restore only one table, then only its data
pg_restore -d app_restored -t orders --schema-only app.dump
pg_restore -d app_restored -t orders --data-only   app.dump

data.title: Interview angle: logical vs physical backups
data.text: `pg_dump` is logical: it exports SQL-level objects and data, so it can restore into a different major version, a different architecture, or a single table, but it is slower and cannot recover to an arbitrary second. Physical backups (base backup plus WAL, or `pg_basebackup`) are byte-for-byte copies of the cluster and enable point-in-time recovery, but are tied to the same major version. Production usually runs both: logical dumps for portability and selective restores, physical backups for fast full recovery and PITR.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Always use `-Fc` (custom format) for pg_dump to allow selective table restores.
Use `-j` (jobs) to parallelize dump and restore across multiple CPU cores.
`pg_dump` takes a non-blocking snapshot using `REPEATABLE READ` transactions.
